overridden_by.because: Bedrock clients prefer AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK over the AWS credential chain, in every client measured, so the aws-auth service behind the pointer is never asked and the jail authenticates with a bearer frozen at launch.

the AWS credential chain reads a static AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID + AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY pair (its environment provider) before the container-credentials pointer in every consumer measured (claude, codex, opencode, pi), so the service is never asked and the jail signs with the long-lived key, neither narrowed nor refreshed.

an AWS SDK reads ~/.aws (its shared-config provider) before the container-credentials pointer, so when ~/.aws holds credentials for the profile the SDK resolves, the jail uses those — the whole permission set, a refresh token included — and the narrowed, refreshing service is skipped while everything looks like it works. A ~/.aws with no credentials for that profile, such as a region-only config, is skipped and the pointer serves; the grant's path cannot say which of the two this is, so the override is possible rather than certain.

description: One machine-wide owner for AWS SSO-backed credentials, minted per profile and narrowed before they reach a jail.
name: aws-auth
